text:
**Lesson Plan: Causes of the First World War** **Class:** Year 9 (34 students) **Duration:** 50 minutes **Curriculum Link:** KS3 History, National Curriculum: "challenges for Britain, Europe and the wider world 1901-present… the First World War… the inter-war years." **Room:** Projector, no student devices. Limited printing (1 A4 sheet per student). **Differentiation:** Wide attainment spread, including 6 students with reading ages below 9. --- ### **Lesson Objectives** *All students will:* - Identify the four main long-term causes of WWI using the acronym M.A.I.N. - Describe the short-term trigger: the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand. *Most students will:* - Explain how the long-term causes created a 'powder keg' in Europe. *Some students will:* - Analyse which long-term cause they consider most significant and justify their view. --- ### **Resources** 1. **Projector & PowerPoint:** Slides with minimal text, key images, and clear visuals. 2. **Printed A4 Sheet (1 per student):** See attached design. Uses a structured, visual template with icons, key word banks, and sentence starters to support lower-reading-age students. 3. **Whiteboard & pens.** 4. **Sticky notes (one per pair of students).** --- ### **Lesson Structure & Timings** **Part 1: Starter – The Spark (5 mins)** - **0-5 mins:** Display a dramatic image of the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand (June 1914). Ask: *"What is happening in this picture? How could one event like this start a world war?"* Class discussion to elicit prior knowledge and introduce the concept of long-term vs. short-term causes. **Part 2: Teacher Exposition – The "Powder Keg" (15 mins)** - **5-20 mins:** Use PowerPoint to introduce the M.A.I.N. causes. **Minimal text on slides.** Use icons and maps. - **Militarism:** Image of the *Dreadnought*; graph of military spending. - **Alliances:** Animated map showing Triple Entente vs. Triple Alliance. - **Imperialism:** Map of colonial empires; cartoon about rivalry (e.g., "The Rhodes Colossus"). - **Nationalism:** Image of Serbian nationalist group logo; quote about pride. - **Teaching Strategy:** Pause after each cause. Ask a quick "thumbs up/middle/down" check for understanding. Use simple, direct language. Repeat key phrases. **Part 3: Structured Activity – Applying M.A.I.N. (20 mins)** - **20-25 mins:** Distribute the **printed A4 sheet**. Read through the instructions and word bank as a class. **Model** completing the first cause (Militarism) on the board using a sentence starter. - **25-40 mins:** **Differentiated tasks:** - **Core Task (All):** Complete the M.A.I.N. table on the sheet using the word bank and sentence starters. - **Support:** Teacher/TA circulates, focusing on the 6 target students. Read prompts aloud. Encourage use of symbols/drawings in the 'icon' column. - **Challenge (Fast-finishers):** Answer the "Which was most important?" question on the back of the sheet, using the prompt to structure a paragraph. **Part 4: Plenary – Checking Understanding (10 mins)** - **40-45 mins: "Sticky Note Summary."** Students pair up (mix attainment levels). Each pair writes **one** cause on a sticky note *without* using M.A.I.N. letters (e.g., "Countries building huge armies"). They stick it to the board. Teacher quickly sorts/organises them under M/A/I/N headings, addressing misconceptions. - **45-50 mins: Exit Ticket & Bell.** Students turn over their A4 sheet. On the back, they complete: **"Today I learned that WWI started because…"** and **"One question I still have is…"** They hand this in as they leave. This provides a quick written check of understanding for every student and informs the next lesson. --- ### **Printed A4 Sheet Design** **(Front)** **Year 9 History: Why did the First World War start?** **The Spark:** Archduke Franz Ferdinand was assassinated in **June 1914**. But Europe was already a **POWDER KEG**… **The Long-Term Causes – M.A.I.N.** | Cause & Icon | What does it mean? (Use the Word Bank) | How did it help cause war? (Finish the sentences) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **M**ilitarism
[Icon: Simple drawing of a warship] | Countries building huge ________ and ________. | It caused fear because… | | **A**lliances
[Icon: Two linked shields] | Countries making ________ to protect each other. | It meant a small problem could become big because… | | **I**mperialism
[Icon: Globe with flags] | Countries competing for ________ around the world. | It created tension and arguments over… | | **N**ationalism
[Icon: Flexed bicep] | Extreme pride in your ________, believing it's the best. | It made countries aggressive and want to… | **Word Bank:** armies, navies, agreements, empires, colonies, country, fight, bigger. **(Back)** **Challenge Question:** Which **ONE** of the M.A.I.N. causes do you think was *most* important in causing WWI? Explain your choice. *I think ______ was most important because…* **Exit Ticket (Complete in last 5 mins!)** 1. Today I learned that WWI started because… 2. One question I still have is… --- ### **Checking Understanding Before the Bell** 1. **Verbal:** Thumbs up/down during exposition. 2. **Visual & Collaborative:** The sticky note sorting activity provides a whole-class snapshot. 3. **Individual Written:** The **exit ticket** on the back of the A4 sheet is handed in. This is the key check. The teacher can quickly scan responses after the lesson to gauge grasp of objectives and identify common questions/misconceptions (e.g., confusing imperialism and nationalism) for follow-up.
